clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old man presenting with 4-day right hypochondrial pain, right hypochondrial tenderness on exam, elevated inflammatory markers (WBC 12,000/ml, CRP 20 mg/l), and a very high CA 19-9 (2016 U/ml). Initial imaging including CT with IV contrast and Bili-MRI showed suspicious irregular thickening of the gallbladder wall with a porcelain-like appearance. Histopathological examination of a specimen showed ulcerated mucosa surrounded by epithelioid cells mixed with rare giant Langerhans cells but without caseous necrosis, consistent with granulomatous inflammation typical of GT. Microbiological stains or cultures were not reported to exclude infectious causes. Ultrasound imaging and treatment/outcome details were also not documented.
